auditedPrs.notes: Squash 8e2de14. Core port is faithful: a disco Ping over DERP from a known peer is answered with Pong{TxID, Src: 127.3.3.40:<region, uint16-truncated>} addressed to the DERP source node key on the region it arrived on, nothing is learned, Geneve-framed disco over DERP is not handed to the disco handler, and a non-peer source gets no pong. Three divergences remain, all minor: no pong when the local UDP bind failed (Go keeps answering over DERP via blockForeverConn), pong admission requires the netmap to bind the DERP source node key to the sender disco key (Go only needs both to be known independently), and a DERP send failure tears the region connection down (Go logs and continues). Upstream cloned shallow at the ledger pin.

findings.title: Relayed disco Ping is not answered when the local UDP socket bind failed (DERP-only mode)
findings.detail: Upstream: Conn.bindSocket falls back to newBlockForeverConn() on bind failure and the Conn keeps running; processDERPReadResult still routes a disco frame from DERP into handleDiscoMessage, and handlePingLocked pongs over DERP through sendAddr with a DERP destination, which never touches the UDP socket. So a Go node whose UDP bind failed still answers `tailscale ping` from a peer on DERP. Merged: ts_runtime/src/direct.rs degrades to DERP-only with the direct-sock handle left None on bind failure, and ts_runtime/src/multiderp.rs run_derp_once hands every DERP frame to the dataplane when `sock` is None (demux_relayed_disco with None returns all frames as data, no replies). handle_relayed_disco/answer_derp_ping only need the disco key and a verifier, not the socket, so the ping is dropped for a structural reason that upstream does not have. The same shape already applied to CallMeMaybe before this PR; the PR extends it to pings.
findings.upstream: wgengine/magicsock/magicsock.go (bindSocket, newBlockForeverConn fallback; handlePingLocked) and wgengine/magicsock/derp.go (processDERPReadResult) @ e2ed432399c9b0fda7aa14e9eb27784d2d893c55

findings.title: DERP pong admission is stricter than upstream: sender disco key must be bound to the DERP source node key
findings.detail: Upstream: handleDiscoMessage admits a frame when c.peerMap.knownPeerDiscoKey(sender) is true for ANY peer; handlePingLocked with isDerp then sets numNodes = 1 whenever c.peerMap.endpointForNodeKey(derpNodeSrc) succeeds, and pongs. The two checks are independent: a known disco key plus a known DERP source node key is enough, and unambiguousNodeKeyOfPingLocked's result is only used to update epAddr mappings on the non-DERP path. Upstream explicitly tolerates one disco key mapping to several node keys (comment on numNodes: node sharing, users switching accounts). Merged: MagicSock::answer_derp_ping calls verify(sender, Some(src.node_key)), and the runtime verifier (ts_runtime/src/direct.rs verify_binding) resolves the disco key to ONE peer via peer_by_known_disco_key and requires that peer's node key to equal the DERP source. A netmap where two node keys share one disco key (multi-profile machine, node sharing) gets a pong only for the peer the lookup happens to return; upstream pongs both. The PR's DECISIONS acknowledges the extra refusal but scopes it to a relayed-ping attack; the legitimate shared-disco-key case is not covered by the tests.
findings.upstream: wgengine/magicsock/magicsock.go (handleDiscoMessage knownPeerDiscoKey gate; handlePingLocked isDerp/numNodes; unambiguousNodeKeyOfPingLocked) @ e2ed432399c9b0fda7aa14e9eb27784d2d893c55

findings.title: A failed DERP send of the pong ends the region connection; upstream logs and keeps the connection
findings.detail: Upstream: the pong is sent with `go c.sendDiscoMessage(...)`; a DERP write goes through derpWriteChanForRegion to runDerpWriter, where a dc.Send error is logged ("magicsock: derp.Send(%v): %v"), metricSendDERPError is incremented, and the writer loop continues; the receive path is unaffected. Merged: ts_runtime/src/multiderp.rs run_derp_once does `client.send_one(to, &frame).await?` inline in the receive loop, so one failed pong send returns from run_derp_once, drops the region connection and reconnects, and the pong send also blocks the region's receive loop while it is in flight. The PR's DECISIONS states this matches the existing queued-disco relay path; it is consistent with that pre-existing choice but not with upstream.
